decisions.reason: Although the authors view the substantive pattern and statistical significance as consistent and describe the differences as small or negligible for the substantive claim, Axis 1 judges whether the original reported numbers were recovered within rounding or negligible numerical variation. Reconstructing the dataset and ban-intensity variable from the raw DHS and ACHEquity data without the author's code produced different sample sizes (255,104/255,105 vs. 254,764), different intensity summary statistics in Table 3, and materially different regression coefficients and standard errors in Replicated Table 4 across both Stata and Python (e.g., Panel A age at marriage 0.823 vs. 1.003 in Stata and 0.7596 in Python; age at first birth 0.541 vs. 0.69 in Stata and 0.484 in Python; Panel B years of schooling 1.064 vs. 1.251 in Stata and 0.896 in Python; Panel D married before age 18 -0.089 vs. -0.045 in Stata and -0.027 in Python, plus diverging Panel A dependent-variable means between Stata and Python/original).

decisions.quote: Because of the time limit, we did not carry out any additional robustness checks.
decisions.reason: Despite referring to their direct reconstruction of the baseline equation in Stata and Python as testing the robustness of the main results, the authors only re-estimated the original baseline specification and explicitly state that they did not conduct any additional robustness checks.

scope_review.parent_objection: Axis1 first reply codes computational issues from close rather than exact reconstructed sample/statistics. Read exact codebook: negligible numerical differences are compatible with computationally reproducible; do not assume all discrepancies or changed sample sizes imply issues. Source says sample close, summary stats similar, main regressions significance/pattern consistent, effect magnitudes differ by small amounts and only nonsignificant coefficient directions differ. Table4 provides actual original and reconstruction values. Are central numbers recovered within negligible variation or materially unrecovered? Judge supplied tables and authors language, not successful substantive claim alone. Axis2 separately: no additional checks, only same baseline in Python/Stata. Return both requested axes; no third call.

prior_reply.quote: We obtain a sample size close to the paper, with some countries having slightly more observations than the paper, suggesting that we may lack certain data-cleaning procedures during the replication. However, the results of our summary statistics are similar to those in the tables.
prior_reply.reason: Reconstructing the analysis from the raw data did not recover the exact reported sample sizes, summary statistics, or regression coefficients, even though the substantive significance pattern remained similar.
